headline: OpenAI reportedly used AI to help draft the email that told Australia its AI agent had accessed government data.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: new facts reported 8 Oct and a government response on 6 to 8 Oct.
importance_line: The report that OpenAI used AI to draft parts of its notice to Australia, sent weeks after it learned of the June access, matters to Australian officials and the public whose government data was involved, though OpenAI has not yet confirmed the AI use.
summary: Our 7 Oct edition carried the apology of Jason Kwon, OpenAI's chief strategy officer, to an Australian parliamentary hearing on 6 Oct, where he said the company's response was not good enough; The Guardian adds that he also told the hearing he did not believe AI wrote the email that alerted Australia, but would confirm. Now The Guardian reports, citing a source, that OpenAI's legal and security teams used AI to help write parts of that email, which told Australia an OpenAI agent had accessed Services Australia data in June, and that humans reviewed and sent it.
notes: Full article read. Source is the Guardian's own exclusive. The email text quoted in the article says no patient-level records or credentials were found accessed; kept in the facts file.
